title: Wake image
description: A deep-blue sea photograph bends under short-lived wave fronts left by a moving pointer.
useCase: Add a local refractive wake to a still image without a simulation package.
interaction: Move across the water and adjust the wake strength.
reducedMotion: The photograph remains still; the distortion strength resolves to zero.
limitations: Twelve analytic pointer marks form the wake; this is not a fluid solver. WebGL 1 is optional, with the original photograph retained underneath.
look: Full-bleed aerial photograph of turquoise surf breaking over rust-red rocks, with white letterspaced caps header, a white range slider and a translucent pill button.
motion: Pointer movement (or touch drag) drops up to twelve marks that each emit an expanding ring wave, refracting the photo for 2.6 s as it fades; a slider scales strength.
adapt: The wake is the `fragment` shader: each of `marks[12]` emits a ring with `front=age*.16` decaying by `exp(-age*1.9)` over `2.6` s; `move` writes marks every `18` ms. Tune `strength` and replace `coastal-break.webp` in both the `img` and `image.src`.
